blocks.en: Unit 2 · Adam, Eve, and the Fall
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 2 · Adán, Eva y la Caída

blocks.en: 1. Adam from Adamah: Dust and Divinity
blocks.es_reference: 1. Adán de Adamah: Polvo y Divinidad

blocks.en: Genesis 2 gives us the detailed narrative of humanity's physical creation. The Hebrew pun is profound: Adam (man) is formed from adamah (ground). The word translated "formed" refers to a master potter creating a masterpiece — careful, deliberate, beautiful. But then God does something breathtaking. He breathes into Adam's nostrils the "breath of life," literally making him a living soul. Humanity is therefore equal parts dust and divinity. The dust humbles us — we are made of the same stuff as the ground beneath our feet. The divine breath dignifies us — we have direct access to God Himself. Every counseling session, every funeral, every birth you attend as a pastor turns on this paradox.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 2 nos da la narrativa detallada de la creación física de la humanidad. El juego de palabras hebreo es profundo: Adán (hombre) es formado de adamah (tierra). La palabra traducida como "formó" se refiere a un maestro alfarero creando una obra maestra — cuidadosa, deliberada, hermosa. Pero luego Dios hace algo impresionante. Sopla en la nariz de Adán el "aliento de vida", literalmente haciéndolo un alma viviente. La humanidad es por tanto partes iguales de polvo y divinidad. El polvo nos humilla — somos del mismo material que el suelo bajo nuestros pies. El aliento divino nos dignifica — tenemos acceso directo al mismo Dios. Cada sesión de consejería, cada funeral, cada nacimiento al que asistirás como pastor gira sobre esta paradoja.

blocks.en: Genesis 2:7 (NKJV): "And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living being."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 2:7 (RVG): "Entonces Jehová Dios formó al hombre del polvo de la tierra, y sopló en su nariz aliento de vida, y fue el hombre un ser viviente."

blocks.en: 2. The Garden: Two Trees, One Command
blocks.es_reference: 2. El Jardín: Dos Árboles, Un Mandamiento

blocks.en: God planted a garden in Eden and placed the man there. The Hebrew word for the garden suggests an enclosed paradise. In the center stood two trees: the Tree of Life and the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil. The Hebrew word for "knowledge" here is experiential — to know something firsthand, by tasting it. God's command was simple: eat freely from any tree, except the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil, "for in the day that you eat of it you shall surely die." In Scripture, death means separation from God. Since no evil dwells in God, to eat from that tree would necessarily separate humanity from the source of life. The command was protection, not restriction.
blocks.es_reference: Dios plantó un jardín en Edén y puso al hombre allí. La palabra hebrea para el jardín sugiere un paraíso cercado. En el centro estaban dos árboles: el Árbol de la Vida y el Árbol del Conocimiento del Bien y del Mal. La palabra hebrea para "conocimiento" aquí es experiencial — saber algo de primera mano, probándolo. El mandamiento de Dios era simple: come libremente de cualquier árbol, excepto del Árbol del Conocimiento del Bien y del Mal, "porque el día que de él comas, ciertamente morirás". En la Escritura, muerte significa separación de Dios. Puesto que ningún mal mora en Dios, comer de ese árbol necesariamente separaría a la humanidad de la fuente de la vida. El mandamiento era protección, no restricción.

blocks.en: 3. The Helper Suitable: Equal and Corresponding
blocks.es_reference: 3. La Ayuda Idónea: Igual y Correspondiente

blocks.en: God said, "It is not good that man should be alone; I will make a helper suitable for him." The word "helper" (ezer) is used throughout the Old Testament to refer to God Himself (Psalm 33:20; 70:5). It implies no subordination. "Suitable" means corresponding and equal — face-to-face. God then brought animals to Adam to name, but no suitable helper was found. So God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam, took a rib from his side, and fashioned the woman. Adam's response — "bone of my bones, flesh of my flesh" — celebrates full equality. The two become "one flesh," a phrase that strongly implies physical union in utter innocence. Adam and his wife were naked and felt no shame.
blocks.es_reference: Dijo Dios: "No es bueno que el hombre esté solo; le haré ayuda idónea para él". La palabra "ayuda" (ezer) se usa en todo el Antiguo Testamento para referirse al mismo Dios (Salmo 33:20; 70:5). No implica subordinación. "Idónea" significa correspondiente e igual — cara a cara. Luego Dios trajo animales a Adán para que los nombrara, pero no se encontró ayuda idónea. Entonces Dios causó un sueño profundo en Adán, tomó una costilla de su costado y formó a la mujer. La respuesta de Adán — "hueso de mis huesos, carne de mi carne" — celebra la igualdad plena. Los dos se convierten en "una sola carne", una frase que implica fuertemente unión física en completa inocencia. Adán y su esposa estaban desnudos y no se avergonzaban.

blocks.en: Pastoral Note: The world tells you that sexuality is shameful, dangerous, or merely biological. Scripture says it was God's idea, given in innocence, to be celebrated within covenant. Preach that without flinching.
blocks.es_reference: Nota Pastoral: El mundo te dice que la sexualidad es vergonzosa, peligrosa o meramente biológica. La Escritura dice que fue idea de Dios, dada en inocencia, para ser celebrada dentro del pacto. Predica eso sin titubear.

blocks.en: 4. The Tempter's Strategy: Subvert, Pervert, Invert
blocks.es_reference: 4. La Estrategia del Tentador: Subvertir, Pervertir, Invertir

blocks.en: The serpent was more cunning than any animal of the field. Take note of this: evil is neither self-existent nor created. Therefore evil is not natural. And being not natural, evil cannot create. What it can do is subvert, pervert, and invert. Subversion twists what is good. Perversion corrupts it. Inversion turns it into its horrific opposite. An example of inversion you may know: a parent should never have to bury a child. When that happens, the grief never fully resolves on this side of heaven. The Fall is an inversion on cosmic scale — humanity, made to receive instruction from God, instead took instruction from a creature it was supposed to rule. The order of creation was flipped on its head.
blocks.es_reference: La serpiente era más astuta que cualquier animal del campo. Toma nota de esto: el mal no es autoexistente ni creado. Por lo tanto, el mal no es natural. Y al no ser natural, el mal no puede crear. Lo que puede hacer es subvertir, pervertir e invertir. La subversión tuerce lo bueno. La perversión lo corrompe. La inversión lo convierte en su opuesto horrible. Un ejemplo de inversión que quizás conozcas: un padre nunca debería tener que enterrar a un hijo. Cuando eso ocurre, el dolor nunca se resuelve completamente de este lado del cielo. La Caída es una inversión a escala cósmica — la humanidad, hecha para recibir instrucción de Dios, en cambio tomó instrucción de una criatura que se suponía debía gobernar. El orden de la creación fue volteado de cabeza.

blocks.en: 5. The Temptation: Adding to God's Word
blocks.es_reference: 5. La Tentación: Añadir a la Palabra de Dios

blocks.en: The serpent asked Eve, "Has God indeed said, 'You shall not eat from any tree of the garden'?" Eve replied correctly that they could eat from the trees but not from the tree in the middle, adding the words: "nor shall you touch it, lest you die." God had never said anything about touching. How often do we add prohibitions God never gave, thinking we are being more holy? Such additions always make God's commands seem arbitrary and harsh — opening the door to doubt. The serpent then flatly contradicted God: "You will not surely die." Then he suggested God was holding back: "God knows that in the day you eat, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God." Notice carefully — when the serpent approached Eve, Adam was right there with her. The text says she "gave to her husband who was with her, and he ate." Adam was not deceived; he chose to follow Eve into sin rather than protect her from it. Eve was deceived; Adam was negligent. This is why the New Testament traces our fall through Adam (Romans 5:12), not Eve. He was the federal head, and he failed his post.
blocks.es_reference: La serpiente preguntó a Eva: "¿Conque Dios os ha dicho: No comáis de todo árbol del huerto?" Eva respondió correctamente que podían comer de los árboles, pero no del árbol en medio, añadiendo las palabras: "ni lo tocaréis, para que no muráis". Dios nunca había dicho nada sobre tocar. ¿Con qué frecuencia añadimos prohibiciones que Dios nunca dio, pensando que somos más santos? Esas adiciones siempre hacen que los mandamientos de Dios parezcan arbitrarios y duros — abriendo la puerta a la duda. Luego la serpiente contradijo directamente a Dios: "No moriréis". Luego sugirió que Dios estaba reteniendo algo: "Sabe Dios que el día que comáis de él, serán abiertos vuestros ojos, y seréis como Dios". Nota cuidadosamente — cuando la serpiente se acercó a Eva, Adán estaba ahí con ella. El texto dice que ella "dio también a su marido, el cual comió así como ella". Adán no fue engañado; él eligió seguir a Eva en el pecado en lugar de protegerla de él. Eva fue engañada; Adán fue negligente. Por eso el Nuevo Testamento rastrea nuestra caída a través de Adán (Romanos 5:12), no de Eva. Él era la cabeza federal, y falló en su puesto.

blocks.en: 6. The Immediate Consequences: Shame and Hiding
blocks.es_reference: 6. Las Consecuencias Inmediatas: Vergüenza y Esconderse

blocks.en: The eyes of both were opened, and they knew they were naked. Innocence was instantly replaced by shame. They sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves — humanity's first attempt at self-righteousness, and it never works. Not only were they ill at ease with each other; when they heard God walking in the garden in the cool of the day, they hid from His presence. The God who had walked with them was now someone to flee. But note: God came seeking them. "Where are you?" He called. That question echoes through every generation — not because God doesn't know, but because He invites us to stop hiding. Every gospel call you will ever issue is an echo of that first divine pursuit.
blocks.es_reference: Fueron abiertos los ojos de ambos, y supieron que estaban desnudos. La inocencia fue reemplazada instantáneamente por la vergüenza. Cosieron hojas de higuera para cubrirse — el primer intento de la humanidad por la auto-justicia, y nunca funciona. No solo estaban incómodos el uno con el otro; cuando oyeron a Dios caminando en el jardín en el fresco del día, se escondieron de Su presencia. El Dios que había caminado con ellos era ahora alguien de quien huir. Pero nota: Dios vino buscándolos. "¿Dónde estás?" llamó. Esa pregunta resuena en cada generación — no porque Dios no sepa, sino porque nos invita a dejar de escondernos. Cada llamado del evangelio que harás es un eco de aquella primera búsqueda divina.

blocks.en: 7. The Curse: Inversions Multiplied
blocks.es_reference: 7. La Maldición: Inversiones Multiplicadas

blocks.en: God pronounced consequences:
blocks.es_reference: Dios pronunció consecuencias:

blocks.en: The serpent: It crawls on its belly. Enmity is placed between its offspring and the woman's Seed. This is the protoevangelium — the first gospel promise. The Seed (Christ) will bruise the serpent's head; the serpent will bruise His heel. A bruised heel heals; a crushed head is fatal. The cross is hidden right here in Genesis 3.
blocks.es_reference: La serpiente: Se arrastra sobre su vientre. La enemistad es puesta entre su simiente y la Simiente de la mujer. Este es el protoevangelio — la primera promesa del evangelio. La Simiente (Cristo) herirá la cabeza de la serpiente; la serpiente herirá Su calcañar. Un calcañar herido sana; una cabeza aplastada es fatal. La cruz está oculta aquí mismo, en Génesis 3.

blocks.en: The woman: Pain multiplied in childbirth. Her desire will be for her husband, and he will rule over her. Hierarchy enters where partnership stood — not by God's original design but as a protective structure in a fallen world.
blocks.es_reference: La mujer: Dolor multiplicado en el parto. Su deseo será para su marido, y él gobernará sobre ella. La jerarquía entra donde estuvo la sociedad — no por el diseño original de Dios sino como estructura protectora en un mundo caído.

blocks.en: The man: The ground is cursed because of him. Thorns and thistles. Sweat. Death — until he returns to the dust from which he was taken.
blocks.es_reference: El hombre: La tierra es maldita por su causa. Espinas y cardos. Sudor. Muerte — hasta que vuelva al polvo del cual fue tomado.

blocks.en: Genesis 3:15 (NKJV): "And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her Seed; He shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise His heel."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 3:15 (RVG): "Y pondré enemistad entre ti y la mujer, y entre tu simiente y la simiente suya; ésta te herirá en la cabeza, y tú le herirás en el calcañar."

blocks.en: 8. God's Mercy in Judgment: Garments of Skin
blocks.es_reference: 8. La Misericordia de Dios en el Juicio: Vestiduras de Piel

blocks.en: The Lord God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife and clothed them. Think of the horror — Adam and Eve had never seen death. Was the sacrificed animal a favorite? Whatever it was, they now understood: sin requires a substitute. A covering that cannot be self-made. This is the first sacrifice, foreshadowing every altar, every lamb, and finally the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world. Then God drove them from the garden, guarding the Tree of Life with cherubim and a flaming sword. This was mercy. To live forever in a fallen state would be the deepest curse imaginable. Better to die and be restored than to live eternally broken.
blocks.es_reference: Jehová Dios hizo vestiduras de piel para Adán y su esposa y los vistió. Piensa en el horror — Adán y Eva nunca habían visto la muerte. ¿Era el animal sacrificado uno de sus favoritos? Lo que fuera, ahora entendieron: el pecado requiere un sustituto. Una cobertura que no puede ser hecha por uno mismo. Este es el primer sacrificio, presagiando cada altar, cada cordero, y finalmente el Cordero de Dios que quita el pecado del mundo. Luego Dios los echó del jardín, guardando el Árbol de la Vida con querubines y una espada ardiente. Esto fue misericordia. Vivir para siempre en un estado caído sería la maldición más profunda imaginable. Mejor morir y ser restaurado que vivir eternamente quebrantado.

blocks.en: 9. Cain and Abel: Worship Rejected, Anger Unmastered
blocks.es_reference: 9. Caín y Abel: Adoración Rechazada, Ira No Dominada

blocks.en: Eve gave birth to Cain, saying, "I have acquired a man with the help of the Lord" — though the Hebrew can also read "Like God I have made a man." A phrase tinged with pride. Abel was a keeper of flocks, aligned with God's original purpose for stewardship. Cain worked the ground, now aligned with the curse. Both brought offerings. Abel brought firstborn of his flock and their fat portions — the best he had, by faith. Cain brought some fruit — discharging a duty without devotion. The Lord regarded Abel's offering but not Cain's. The problem was not the type of offering but the attitude behind it. Cain became furious. God warned him: "Sin is crouching at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it." Cain did not master it. He killed Abel — the first human death, another cosmic inversion. When God asked where Abel was, Cain shot back, "Am I my brother's keeper?" The answer, then and now, is yes. God placed a mark on Cain to protect him from vengeance, and Cain went out from the presence of the Lord and settled in the land of Nod — which means "wandering."
blocks.es_reference: Eva dio a luz a Caín, diciendo: "He adquirido un varón con la ayuda del Señor" — aunque el hebreo también puede leerse "Como Dios he hecho un hombre". Una frase teñida de orgullo. Abel era pastor de ovejas, alineado con el propósito original de Dios de mayordomía. Caín labraba la tierra, ahora alineado con la maldición. Ambos trajeron ofrendas. Abel trajo primogénitos de su rebaño y la grasa de ellos — lo mejor que tenía, por fe. Caín trajo algunos frutos — cumpliendo un deber sin devoción. Jehová miró con agrado la ofrenda de Abel pero no la de Caín. El problema no era el tipo de ofrenda sino la actitud detrás de ella. Caín se enfureció. Dios le advirtió: "El pecado está a la puerta; su deseo será para ti, pero tú debes dominarlo". Caín no lo dominó. Mató a Abel — la primera muerte humana, otra inversión cósmica. Cuando Dios preguntó dónde estaba Abel, Caín respondió: "¿Soy yo guarda de mi hermano?" La respuesta, entonces y ahora, es sí. Dios puso una marca en Caín para protegerlo de la venganza, y Caín salió de la presencia del Señor y se estableció en la tierra de Nod — que significa "vagabundeo".

blocks.en: 10. Seth and the Hope of the Godly Line
blocks.es_reference: 10. Set y la Esperanza de la Línea Piadosa

blocks.en: Genesis 4 ends with a strange contrast. The line of Cain produces Lamech, who boasts of vengeance multiplied — "If Cain is avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy-sevenfold." Sin is accelerating, not just continuing. But against this dark backdrop, Adam and Eve had another son, Seth, meaning "appointed." He was given in place of Abel. With Seth's son Enosh, men began to call upon — or better, proclaim — the name of the Lord. Despite the horror of the Fall, the murder of Abel, and the growing corruption, God preserved a line of those who would worship Him. The promise of Genesis 3:15 was still alive. The whole sweep of Genesis 4 is the divergence of two lines: those who exalt themselves and those who worship God. The same divergence will define every page that follows — and every congregation you will ever pastor.
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 4 termina con un contraste extraño. La línea de Caín produce a Lamec, que se jacta de venganza multiplicada — "Si siete veces será vengado Caín, Lamec en verdad setenta veces siete lo será". El pecado se acelera, no solo continúa. Pero contra ese trasfondo oscuro, Adán y Eva tuvieron otro hijo, Set, que significa "designado". Fue dado en lugar de Abel. Con el hijo de Set, Enós, los hombres comenzaron a invocar — o mejor, proclamar — el nombre del Señor. A pesar del horror de la Caída, el asesinato de Abel y la creciente corrupción, Dios preservó una línea de aquellos que lo adorarían. La promesa de Génesis 3:15 seguía viva. Toda la trayectoria de Génesis 4 es la divergencia de dos líneas: aquellos que se exaltan a sí mismos y aquellos que adoran a Dios. La misma divergencia definirá cada página que sigue — y cada congregación que pastorearás algún día.

mc.stem: What Hebrew pun explains the name 'Adam'?
mc.why: Correct. Adam from adamah — humanity from the ground, a deliberate Hebrew wordplay binding us to the soil from which we were taken.

mc.stem: The word translated 'formed' in Genesis 2:7 pictures God as what?
mc.why: Yes. God is depicted as a master potter — careful, deliberate, crafting a masterpiece.

mc.stem: What did God breathe into Adam's nostrils?
options: The breath of life / living soul
mc.why: Correct. The breath of life made Adam a living soul — equal parts dust and divinity.

mc.stem: The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil offered what kind of 'knowledge'?
mc.why: Yes. The Hebrew word da'at implies knowing by experience, firsthand — not abstract learning.

mc.stem: In Scripture, what does 'death' primarily mean?
mc.why: Correct. Death is separation from God, who is the source of life. Physical death follows but is not primary.

mc.stem: The word 'helper' (ezer) in Genesis 2:18 is used elsewhere in the OT to refer to whom?
mc.why: Excellent. Ezer is used of God (Psalm 33:20) — no subordination implied. God is our helper.

mc.stem: What does 'one flesh' in Genesis 2:24 strongly imply?
mc.why: Yes. Physical union within marriage, in utter innocence and without shame — God's design from the start.

mc.stem: What three actions describe evil's power since it cannot create?
mc.why: Correct. Evil subverts (twists good), perverts (corrupts), and inverts (turns into the opposite).

mc.stem: What did Eve add to God's command when speaking to the serpent?
mc.why: Yes. God never said anything about touching. Adding to God's word made His command seem arbitrary and harsh.

mc.stem: After eating the fruit, what was the immediate result?
options: They knew they were naked and felt shame
mc.why: Correct. Innocence was replaced by shame — they hid from each other and from God.

mc.stem: What is the protoevangelium (first gospel promise) in Genesis 3:15?
options: The Seed of the woman will crush the serpent's head
mc.why: Yes! The Seed (Christ) will crush the serpent's head — the first promise of redemption, hidden in the curse itself.

mc.stem: What did God make for Adam and Eve after the Fall?
mc.why: Correct. Garments of skin required an animal's death — the first sacrifice, foreshadowing Christ.

mc.stem: Why did God drive humanity from the Garden and guard the Tree of Life?
options: To prevent eternal life in a fallen state
mc.why: Correct. Living forever broken and fallen would be a curse, not a blessing. The expulsion was mercy.

mc.stem: What did Cain's name mean according to Eve's prideful statement?
options: 'Like God I have made a man'
mc.why: Yes. 'Like God I have made a man' — revealing pride right from birth.

mc.stem: Why did God reject Cain's offering but accept Abel's?
mc.why: Correct. The issue was not the offering type but Cain's heart attitude. God looks at the heart, not the gift.

mc.stem: What did God warn Cain about sin before he killed Abel?
options: 'Sin is crouching at the door; you must master it'
mc.why: Yes. God gave Cain a clear warning and an opportunity to repent. Sin must be mastered, not negotiated with.

mc.stem: Where did Cain settle after being cursed?
mc.why: Correct. Nod means 'wandering' — ironic for one who 'settled' there. Sin produces restlessness.

mc.stem: What does the name 'Seth' mean?
mc.why: Yes. Seth was appointed in place of Abel — a sign that God's purposes were not defeated.

mc.stem: What did people begin to do in the time of Enosh, Seth's son?
options: Call upon / proclaim the name of the Lord
mc.why: Correct. Even amid corruption, a faithful line began to publicly worship and proclaim the Lord's name.

mc.stem: What did the garments of skin foreshadow?
mc.why: Yes. Every altar and every lamb pointed forward to the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.

sa.prompt: Explain what it means that humanity is 'equal parts dust and divinity.'
sa.model: We are formed from the ground (dust to humble us) and breathed with God's own breath (divinity giving us access to Him).

sa.prompt: What does the word 'helper' (ezer) tell us about the woman's status and role?
sa.model: Ezer is used of God Himself; it implies strength and support, not subordination. Woman is equal to man.

sa.prompt: Explain the three strategies of evil: subvert, pervert, invert.
sa.model: Evil cannot create, so it subverts (twists good), perverts (corrupts), and inverts (turns into its opposite).

sa.prompt: What did Eve add to God's command, and why was that dangerous?
sa.model: Eve added 'nor shall you touch it,' making God's command seem arbitrary and opening the doorway to doubt.

sa.prompt: What is the protoevangelium and why is it significant?
sa.model: The first gospel promise — the Seed of the woman (Christ) will crush the serpent's head. Redemption announced in the very curse.

sa.prompt: Why were the garments of skin an act of mercy, not just judgment?
sa.model: God provided a covering that required an innocent substitute's death — mercy and foreshadowing of Christ.

sa.prompt: Why did God guard the Tree of Life after the Fall?
sa.model: Living forever in a fallen, sinful state would be a curse. God showed mercy by preventing eternal brokenness.

sa.prompt: What was the difference between Cain's and Abel's offerings, and why did God reject Cain's?
sa.model: Abel brought the best by faith; Cain merely discharged a duty. God looks at the heart, not just the gift.

sa.prompt: What does the land of Nod signify about Cain's spiritual state?
sa.model: Nod means 'wandering.' Cain left God's presence — alienation and restlessness without repentance.

sa.prompt: What hope remained after the tragedy of Cain and Abel?
sa.model: Seth was appointed in Abel's place, and his descendants began to call on the Lord — the promise lived on.
